links.source_location: file is 19 lines of pure whitespace — likely a spacer so animated frames occupy the logo area, but purpose is not stated anywhere
lines 97, 148 — hyprctl keyword does not work under the Lua provider
line 139 — why pixelSize values were hardcoded down instead
line 151 restates line 71 as a Lua-config gotcha
line 79 — every dashboard panel re-themes from the pywal palette
both repurpose a terminal window as a purely decorative surface rather than an interactive shell
both apply a theme conf to kitty — one persistently via include, one ephemerally via remote control
both re-color a running environment without restarting it — pywal regeneration vs kitty remote-control set-colors
both achieve the same frosted-glass look via transparency + blur, one through window rules and one through layer rules
root README describes the custom fastfetch ASCII that .config/fastfetch holds
dashboard autolaunches apps onto workspace 1 via exec_cmd, the exact mechanism line 149 warns about
line 124 — 'randomized bold keyboard characters (# @ % & $ *)' matches the glyph set used in the Au5 ASCII asset
both use the fastfetch $1 color placeholder as interchangeable logo assets
maintainer-side generation steps vs contributor-side PR steps for the same 'add a theme' outcome
same failure mode in two different upstream projects: a documented config option that is not actually wired to behavior, forcing a manual override
line 1 color placeholder: $1 vs ${c1}; literal $ doubled to $$ for fastfetch escaping
PR template duplicates the issue template's YAML frontmatter (name/title/labels/assignees: dexpota) verbatim — frontmatter is meaningless in a PR template, so this looks like a copy-paste
